textDevices: One row per device. The IP address is enough; the MAC address is filled in by the search and lets the adapter follow the device if its address changes. Supported: all Mill Generation 3 devices with local API (panel, convection and oil heaters, Wi-Fi Socket).
textDiscover: Mill devices do not announce themselves on the network. The search asks every address of the given network for the Mill status page. Found devices are added to the table above - save afterwards.
helpNetworks: e.g. 192.168.1.0/24 or 192.168.1.100-192.168.1.150; several separated by commas. Empty = the /24 network of the first device.
helpDiscover: Takes up to half a minute for a /24 network. The instance must be running.
labelRediscover: Look for a device again if it stops answering
helpRediscover: Needs the MAC address in the table. At most once every 30 minutes per device.
helpPollInterval: Temperature, power, mode. The devices cannot push changes.
helpSlowInterval: Locks, calibration, preset temperatures and other rarely changing values.
helpTimeout: A device counts as offline after three failed polls in a row.
textControl: On by default. Every value exists once and shows the device value; control.* and settings.* can be written directly (incl. weekly program, timers and vacation as JSON) and are checked before sending. ON always switches on: manual mode 'Switch', relay closed, regardless of thermostat, weekly program and target temperature. OFF always switches off: in 'Switch' the relay opens, in every other mode the device goes to 'Off'. To heat by thermostat again, choose an operation mode such as 'Control individually'.
helpAllowControl: Switching it off makes control.* and settings.* read-only.
textApiKey: Only for devices on which an API key was set: they then answer via HTTPS with a self-signed certificate (not verified) and expect the key with every request. Tick 'API key' in the device row. The adapter never sets a key itself - removing one requires a factory reset of the device.
helpApiKey: Stored encrypted. Used for all devices with 'API key' ticked.
textNetwork: The local API works without internet. In the operation mode 'Control individually' the device simply follows its target temperature; the weekly program and timers need the correct time, which the device only gets from the internet after each restart (it has no battery-backed clock). Use a DHCP reservation so the address stays the same.
textCloud: The adapter does not need the Mill cloud or app. Whether the device talks to the cloud is shown in settings.cloudCommunication and status.cloudConnected.
textDocker: Works in a bridge network: the adapter only opens outgoing HTTP connections. No port mapping is needed.
textEnergy: The devices report only the momentary power. energy.* is calculated from it between two polls - an estimate, gaps (device offline, adapter stopped) are not counted.
labelSyncTimezone: Keep the device's time zone in line with ioBroker
helpSyncTimezone: Needed for weekly program, timers and vacation; follows daylight saving time. The device takes the time itself via NTP from pool.ntp.org – without internet point that name to a local NTP server (e.g. a DNS rewrite).
